senses.example: The bright red chair jars with the quiet room.
senses.exampleCN: 那张鲜红的椅子与安静的房间很不协调。
senses.why: A harsh sound in a soft place is the metaphor behind this social sense.
senses.whyCN: 柔和之处的一声刺响，正是这个比喻义的底子。

intro.en: Jar for a container came through French jarre from Arabic jarrah, while the verb of knocking is an English imitation of a harsh sound.
intro.cn: 表示容器的 jar 经法语 jarre 来自阿拉伯语 jarrah；表示撞响的动词则是英语对刺耳声音的模仿。

items.en: jarrah named a large earthen water pot.
items.cn: jarrah 指大的陶制水罐。

items.en: Spanish jarra and jarro carried the word in the same sense.
items.cn: 西班牙语 jarra、jarro 带着同样的意义流传。

items.en: Old French jarre meant a jar or ewer.
items.cn: 古法语 jarre 意为罐、水壶。

items.en: English borrowed jar for a clay or glass vessel.
items.cn: 英语借入 jar，指陶制或玻璃容器。

items.en: The verb jar, to knock or grate, developed separately.
items.cn: 表示撞击、摩擦出声的动词 jar 是另外发展的。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jar- family; the near-meaning group holds containers and harsh sounds.
note.cn: 形近组是 jar- 词族；近义组收容器与刺耳声相关词。

entries.definition: The amount a jar holds.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ful 构成，义为「一罐之量」。

entries.definition: The plural of jar.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，义为「多个罐子」，同族。

entries.definition: Harsh and unpleasant to hear or see.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「刺耳的；令人不安的」。

entries.definition: A container for liquids with a handle and a lip.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「壶」，带把手和倒口。

entries.definition: A metal container for food.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「罐头」，材质是金属。

entries.definition: A narrow-necked container for liquids.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「瓶子」，口窄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks deal with the two histories together: the Arabic pot and the English harsh knock.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把两条历史放在一起：阿拉伯语的罐子与英语的刺耳撞击声。

normal.en: Arabic jarrah was a big water pot.
normal.cn: 阿拉伯语 jarrah 是大的水罐。

normal.en: French jarre and Spanish jarra are cousins.
normal.cn: 法语 jarre 与西班牙语 jarra 是它的亲属。

normal.en: A jarful is the amount one jar holds.
normal.cn: jarful 就是一罐的量。

normal.en: The door jarred against the frame with a bang.
normal.cn: 门在门框上砰地一撞。

normal.en: White walls and a red chair jar with each other.
normal.cn: 白墙和红椅子彼此不协调。

abstract.en: A jar holds something in a round glass body.
abstract.cn: 罐子用圆鼓的玻璃身体把东西装住。

abstract.en: A jarring sound is a noise that refuses to fit.
abstract.cn: 刺耳声是一种拒绝合拍的噪声。

abstract.en: What jars cannot settle into the room around it.
abstract.cn: 不协调的东西安不进周围的房间。

examples.en: Put the pickles in a clean jar.
examples.cn: 把泡菜放进一只干净的罐子。

examples.en: The sudden noise jarred her awake.
examples.cn: 突然的响声把她震醒了。

examples.en: His joke jarred with the serious mood.
examples.cn: 他的笑话与严肃的气氛很不协调。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎」—— 玻璃罐没接住，扎在地上咣一声

root: 阿拉伯语 jarrah「大陶水罐」→ 西班牙语 jarra → 古法语 jarre → 英语 jar「罐子」；动词「撞响、不协调」为英语另行发展。同族有 jarful、jarring。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a wide container, the amount inside, a harsh sound, a physical shake, and being out of harmony.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：广口容器、一罐之量、刺耳声、身体震动，以及与周围不协调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide glass jar, honey at the bottom, its lid askew.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只广口玻璃罐，罐底有蜜，盖子歪着。

branches.en: THE SHELF: morning light through a glass wall.
branches.cn: 架子这条线：晨光透过玻璃壁。

branches.en: THE OLIVES: one whole jar eaten at once.
branches.cn: 橄榄这条线：一次吃完一整罐。

branches.en: THE DOOR: metal grinding on a frame.
branches.cn: 门这条线：金属蹭过门框。

branches.en: THE FALL: a shock felt through the shoulder.
branches.cn: 摔倒这条线：从肩膀透上来的冲击。

branches.en: THE ROOM: a red chair that does not belong.
branches.cn: 房间这条线：格格不入的红椅子。

intro.en: Jar as a container is a borrowing reshaped in English; the endings below are English or Arabic-French spellings.
intro.cn: 表示容器的 jar 是借词在英语里定型；下面的成分包括英语词尾与阿拉伯—法语拼写。

latinIntro.en: The container word travelled through Arabic and Spanish, not Latin; there is no Latin entry for it.
latinIntro.cn: 表示容器的这个词经阿拉伯语和西班牙语传来，不经过拉丁语，因此没有拉丁条目。

items.example: The Spanish form of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的西班牙语形式。

items.example: It comes from the verb jar.
The base noun of the entry.

definition_zh: 颌；下巴；（字面或比喻）下颚；（工具）钳口
definition_en: either of the two bones or parts that form the mouth and hold the teeth, or a gripping part of a tool
core_image: 一张脸的下半部，上下两排牙齿像两把钳子合上
scene: 老人慢慢嚼着面包，脸上的颌骨一起一落。His jaw moved slowly as he chewed.
sceneCN: 这里 jaw 是「颌」（第 1 个义项：构成嘴部、承载牙齿的骨或部位），句意为他咀嚼时下颌慢慢动着。画面里的物件：面包、牙齿、老年斑的皮肤。

pos.zh: 名词：颌；下巴；钳口
动词：喋喋不休（口语）

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「上下颌」，也指机构的夹钳
由 jaw 加 -ed 构成，义为「有……颌的」，见于 long-jawed 等复合词
由 jaw 与 bone 复合，义为「颌骨」

senses.title: The bone that holds teeth
senses.definition: one of the two bony structures that form the frame of the mouth and hold the teeth
senses.definitionCN: 构成嘴部框架并承载牙齿的两块骨结构之一
senses.example: He broke his lower jaw in the match.
senses.exampleCN: 他在比赛中摔断了下颌。
senses.why: The anatomical sense is the oldest and stays the basis for every later use.
senses.whyCN: 解剖义最古老，也是后来所有用法的基础。

senses.title: The lower part of the face
senses.definition: the lower part of the face, seen especially when it is large or firm
senses.definitionCN: 脸的下部，尤其指宽大或坚硬的形态
senses.example: A square jaw ran across the whole bottom of his face.
senses.exampleCN: 宽方的下巴横过他的脸底。
senses.why: The bone shapes the face, so people name the visible outline by the bone beneath.
senses.whyCN: 骨头撑出脸的形状，于是人们用底下的骨来称呼那道外轮廓。

senses.title: A gripping part of a tool
senses.definition: one of the two parts of a vice or wrench that close on an object
senses.definitionCN: 老虎钳或扳手上合拢夹物的两片之一
senses.example: Tighten the jaws of the vice around the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 把老虎钳的钳口夹紧管道。
senses.why: A tool grips with two facing surfaces exactly as a mouth bites with two jaws.
senses.whyCN: 工具用两片相对的面夹住东西，与嘴用上下颌咬住一模一样。

senses.title: Something that closes in
senses.definition: a dangerous opening or closing area, such as between waves or between rocks
senses.definitionCN: 危险的开合处，如巨浪之间或岩石之间
senses.example: The boat slipped into the jaws of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 小船滑进了风暴的夹口。
senses.why: The mouth image grows into any wide, closing gap that swallows what enters.
senses.whyCN: 嘴的意象扩大成任何张开又合拢、把东西吞进去的缺口。

senses.title: To talk on and on
senses.definition: used informally for talking at length, often about nothing important
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示长时间讲话，常指说些不重要的事
senses.example: They jawed about football all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整晚都在聊足球。
senses.why: The verb turns the jaw that does the working into the act of talking.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个干活的颌变成了说话这个动作。

intro.en: Jaw is an old French borrowing, from Old French joue, meaning cheek, reshaped in English toward the sound it names.
intro.cn: jaw 是从古法语借来的词，原形 joue 意为「面颊」，在英语里逐渐定型为现在的读音与拼写。

items.en: joue meant a cheek.
items.cn: joue 意为面颊。

items.en: English took the word as jawe or chaw, and it meant the part that holds teeth.
items.cn: 英语借入为 jawe 或 chaw，指承载牙齿的部位。

items.en: The spelling drifted toward jaw and the meaning settled on the bone.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐变成 jaw，词义固定在骨头上。

items.en: The tool sense appeared as machines with gripping parts spread.
items.cn: 随着带夹持部件的机器普及，工具义出现。

items.en: The informal verb to jaw, meaning to chatter, is recorded from the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 口语动词 jaw「喋喋不休」在十九世纪有记录。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jaw- family; the near-meaning group holds words for mouth parts and gripping tools.
note.cn: 形近组是 jaw- 词族；近义组收嘴部器官与夹持工具相关词。

entries.definition: The two jaws, or a gripping pair.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，义为「上下颌」，也指成对的夹口。

entries.definition: The bone of the jaw.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「颌骨」，同族名词。

entries.definition: So surprising that the mouth falls open.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「令人瞠目结舌的」。

entries.definition: The part of the face below the mouth.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「下巴尖」，只指最外边的一点。

entries.definition: The side of the face below the eye.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「面颊」，jaw 的古法语原义就是它。

entries.definition: A curved gripping part on an animal or tool.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「爪」，指弯曲的夹持部位。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Old French cheek into the bone, the vice, and the storm.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从古法语的「面颊」走到骨头、老虎钳与风暴。

normal.en: Old French joue meant a cheek.
normal.cn: 古法语 joue 意为面颊。

normal.en: English kept the sound and moved the meaning to the bone.
normal.cn: 英语保留了读音，把词义移到了骨头上。

normal.en: A vice has two jaws that close on a pipe.
normal.cn: 老虎钳有两只钳口夹住管道。

normal.en: The jaws of the storm swallow small boats.
normal.cn: 风暴的夹口会吞掉小船。

normal.en: To jaw with friends is to talk for hours.
normal.cn: to jaw with friends 就是聊上几个小时。

abstract.en: A jaw is a clamp built into a face.
abstract.cn: 颌就是长在脸上的一把钳子。

abstract.en: Teeth close; so does a wrench.
abstract.cn: 牙齿会合上，扳手也会。

abstract.en: What opens wide will one day close.
abstract.cn: 张得很大的东西总有一天会合拢。

examples.en: He rubbed his jaw where the ball had hit him.
examples.cn: 他揉了揉被球打中的下巴。

examples.en: The crocodile opened its jaws and waited.
examples.cn: 鳄鱼张开嘴等着。

examples.en: They stood jawing at the corner for an hour.
examples.cn: 他们在街角站着聊了一个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爪」—— 上下颌像一对爪子把食物抓住

root: 古法语 joue「面颊」→ 中古英语 jawe／chaw「承载牙齿的部位」→ 现代英语 jaw「颌；下巴；钳口」。同族有 jaws、jawbone、jaw-dropping。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the bone that holds teeth, the visible lower face, a tool's gripping part, a closing gap, and talking at length.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：承载牙齿的骨、可见的下半脸、工具的夹持部位、张合的缺口，以及长篇闲聊。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the lower half of a face closing two rows of teeth like pliers.
core.cn: 核心意象：脸的下半部，两排牙齿像钳子一样合上。

branches.en: THE MATCH: a lower jaw broken by a fall.
branches.cn: 比赛这条线：摔断的下颌。

branches.en: THE FACE: a square outline under the skin.
branches.cn: 脸这条线：皮下那道方方的轮廓。

branches.en: THE VICE: two steel jaws on a pipe.
branches.cn: 老虎钳这条线：夹住管道的两片钢口。

branches.en: THE SEA: storm jaws around a small boat.
branches.cn: 海这条线：围住小船的暴风夹口。

branches.en: THE CORNER: two friends talking through the evening.
branches.cn: 街角这条线：两人聊过整个晚上。

intro.en: Jaw is a French borrowing reshaped in English; the later forms are English compounds and endings.
intro.cn: jaw 是法语借词在英语里改定的，较晚的形式都是英语复合与词尾。

latinIntro.en: The source is Old French, not Latin, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是古法语而非拉丁语，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.exampleCN: 有文献记载的法语来源。

definition_zh: 爵士乐；爵士舞；爵士风格；（口语）活力、花样
definition_en: a style of music with strong rhythm and free improvisation, developed by African American musicians
core_image: 小号手闭着眼，音符从乐器里甩出去，鼓手在旁跟着改动节奏
scene: 午夜的小酒吧里，几个人轮流即兴，观众用脚打拍子。The band played jazz until two in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 jazz 是「爵士乐」（第 1 个义项：以强烈节奏与即兴为特点的音乐），句意为乐队一直演奏爵士乐到凌晨两点。画面里的物件：酒吧、小号、鼓、打拍的脚。

pos.zh: 名词：爵士乐；活力；花样
动词：（口语）使其更热闹；即兴演奏

derivatives.zh: 由 jazz 加 -y 构成，义为「爵士风格的；花哨的」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「兴奋的」
由 jazz 与 man 复合，义为「爵士乐手」

senses.title: The music itself
senses.definition: a style of music with strong rhythm, swing, and a large share of improvisation
senses.definitionCN: 节奏强烈、摇摆感明显、即兴成分很大的音乐风格
senses.example: Jazz was born in the southern United States.
senses.exampleCN: 爵士乐诞生于美国南部。
senses.why: The musical sense is the core of the word and the source of every other meaning.
senses.whyCN: 音乐义是这个词的核心，也是其他意义之源。

senses.title: The style attached to it
senses.definition: the manner, dress, or way of playing that belongs to jazz performance
senses.definitionCN: 属于爵士演奏的方式、穿着或风格
senses.example: The cafe has a jazz feel with dark wood and warm lights.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆用深色木头和暖灯营造出爵士味。
senses.why: A style can be named by the music it evokes, even when no music is playing.
senses.whyCN: 即使不放音乐，一种风格也可以借它唤起的音乐来命名。

senses.title: A dance to that music
senses.definition: a lively dance performed to jazz music, later a stage dance form
senses.definitionCN: 随爵士乐跳的活泼舞蹈，后来发展成舞台舞种
senses.example: Students learn jazz in the dance class.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在舞蹈课上学习爵士舞。
senses.why: Dancing grew with the music, and the name travelled with the rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 舞蹈随音乐一同成长，名字也随着节奏一起走。

senses.title: Liveliness or energy
senses.definition: an informal use for energy, excitement, or a lively quality in something
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法，指活力、兴奋或某种生动特质
senses.example: The new colours gave the room some jazz.
senses.exampleCN: 新的色彩给房间添了些活力。
senses.why: Jazz as lively music becomes a word for liveliness itself.
senses.whyCN: 爵士乐这种活泼的音乐，本身就成了「活泼」的代称。

senses.title: To make lively
senses.definition: to add decoration or energy to something so that it becomes more interesting
senses.definitionCN: 给某物增添装饰或活力，使其更有趣
senses.example: They jazzed up the menu for the holiday season.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为节日季把菜单做得更花哨。
senses.why: The verb takes the lively quality of the noun and hands it to another thing.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词里那股活泼劲儿交到别的东西身上。

intro.en: Jazz appeared in print around 1912 for baseball slang and by the late 1910s for music; its deeper origin is still disputed.
intro.cn: jazz 约在 1912 年出现在报纸上是棒球俚语，到 1910 年代末指音乐，更深层的来源至今仍有争议。

items.en: Early records of jazz describe energy and liveliness, not yet music.
items.cn: 早期记录里的 jazz 指精力旺盛、活泼，还不是音乐。

items.en: The word spread from California newspapers in the late 1910s.
items.cn: 这个词在 1910 年代末从加州报纸传开。

items.en: New Orleans bands took jazz as the name of their music around 1917.
items.cn: 新奥尔良的乐队约在 1917 年用 jazz 称呼他们的音乐。

items.en: The music came from African American communities, including brass bands and blues.
items.cn: 这种音乐来自非裔美国人社群，包括铜管乐队与蓝调。

items.en: Jazz became a word for its style and later for liveliness in general.
items.cn: jazz 先成为风格之名，后来又泛指活泼。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jazz- family; the near-meaning group holds music styles and related performance words.
note.cn: 形近组是 jazz- 词族；近义组收音乐风格与演出相关词。

entries.definition: In the style of jazz, or bright and showy.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -y 构成，义为「爵士风的；花哨的」。

entries.definition: A musician who plays jazz.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「爵士乐手」，同族名词。

entries.definition: Very excited.
entries.definitionCN: 口语形容词，义为「兴奋的」。

entries.definition: A slow sad music form from African American tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「蓝调」，节奏更慢、情绪更沉。

entries.definition: A strong rhythmic style related to jazz.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「摇摆乐」，是爵士的近亲风格。

entries.definition: To make up music as you play it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「即兴演奏」，是爵士的核心手法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the slang sense of energy to the New Orleans bands.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从俚语里的「活力」走到新奥尔良的乐队。

normal.en: Jazz began as US slang for liveliness.
normal.cn: jazz 起初是美国俚语，指活力。

normal.en: New Orleans bands named the music jazz around 1917.
normal.cn: 新奥尔良乐队约在 1917 年把这种音乐叫作 jazz。

normal.en: Jazzy means in the style of jazz, or showy.
normal.cn: jazzy 意为爵士风的，或花哨的。

normal.en: Jazz up means to give something more life.
normal.cn: jazz up 意为给某物添生气。

normal.en: The deeper origin of jazz is still unknown.
normal.cn: jazz 更深层的来源至今不明。

abstract.en: Jazz is music that changes while you listen.
abstract.cn: 爵士是你听着它就在变的音乐。

abstract.en: A horn throws a line, and the drums answer back.
abstract.cn: 号甩出一句，鼓接回一句。

abstract.en: Liveliness itself can be called jazz.
abstract.cn: 活泼劲儿本身也可以被叫作 jazz。

examples.en: She listens to jazz while she works.
examples.cn: 她工作时听爵士乐。

examples.en: The festival mixes jazz with local folk songs.
examples.cn: 这个音乐节把爵士乐与当地民歌混在一起。

examples.en: They jazzed up the old hall with bright lights.
examples.cn: 他们用明快的灯光让旧礼堂热闹起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎兹」—— 音一扎一响，就是即兴摇摆的味儿

root: 美国俚语 jazz（约 1912 年出现，初指活力）→ 1910 年代末从西海岸报纸传开 → 1917 年前后新奥尔良乐队用于音乐 → 二十世纪扩展为风格与「活力」义。同族有 jazzy、jazzman。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the music, its style, the dance, liveliness, and the verb of making something livelier.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：爵士乐、其风格、爵士舞、活力，以及使更有生气的动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trumpeter improvising while the drummer answers him.
core.cn: 核心意象：小号手即兴，鼓手在旁边回应。

branches.en: THE BANDS: brass, blues, and a rhythm section.
branches.cn: 乐队这条线：铜管、蓝调与节奏组。

branches.en: THE CAFE: dark wood and warm lights with no music playing.
branches.cn: 咖啡馆这条线：深木与暖灯，却不放音乐。

branches.en: THE STUDIO: dancers learning a swing step.
branches.cn: 舞蹈室这条线：学员模仿摇摆步。

branches.cn: 房间这条线：一点让人醒过来的颜色。

definition_zh: 嫉妒的；羡慕的；吃醋的；小心守护的
definition_en: unhappy because someone has something you want, or afraid of losing someone's love or attention
core_image: 有人朝你喜欢的人伸出手，你不由地把杯子握得更紧
scene: 聚会上有人和她聊了很久，他在角落里一直盯着那只杯子。He felt jealous when she laughed with his old friend.
sceneCN: 这里 jealous 是「嫉妒的」（第 1 个义项：因别人得到自己想要的东西而不快），句意为她和他的老朋友说笑时他感到嫉妒。画面里的物件：聚会的杯子、角落、旁人的笑声。

pos.zh: 形容词：嫉妒的；吃醋的；小心守护的

derivatives.zh: 由 jealous 加 -y 构成，义为「嫉妒；吃醋」
由 jealous 加 -ly 构成，义为「嫉妒地；小心地」
由 jealous 加 -ness 构成，义为「嫉妒的状态」

senses.title: Wanting what another has
senses.definition: unhappy and resentful because someone else has something you want
senses.definitionCN: 因别人拥有你想要的东西而不快、怨恨
senses.example: He was jealous of her new car.
senses.exampleCN: 他嫉妒她的新车。
senses.why: This sense grows from the older fear of rivals and is now the commonest use.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项从更古老的「害怕情敌」延伸出来，如今最常用。

senses.title: Afraid of losing love
senses.definition: afraid that someone you love might be more interested in another person
senses.definitionCN: 害怕所爱的人对别人更有兴趣
senses.example: She gets jealous if he talks for long to anyone else.
senses.exampleCN: 只要他跟别人聊久了，她就会吃醋。
senses.why: The rival's jealousy is the oldest thread, kept in the emotional sense we still use.
senses.whyCN: 提防情敌的嫉妒是最古老的一条线，保存在我们今天仍在用的情感义里。

senses.title: Guarding possessively
senses.definition: very careful to protect something you think of as yours
senses.definitionCN: 非常谨慎地守护自己认为是自己的东西
senses.example: The manager is jealous of his team's time.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理很爱惜团队的时间。
senses.why: Guarding closely is the same grip on what one considers one's own, with anger removed.
senses.whyCN: 紧守不放是对「自己之物」的同一种握紧，只是抽掉了愤怒。

senses.title: Envying with respect
senses.definition: admiring another person's good fortune in a way that is slightly painful
senses.definitionCN: 带着一点痛感地羡慕别人的好运
senses.example: I am jealous of your long holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 我羡慕你那么长的假期。
senses.why: In everyday speech the word now covers mild envy as well as resentment.
senses.whyCN: 在日常口语里，这个词既指怨恨，也涵盖轻微的羡慕。

senses.title: Protective of an idea
senses.definition: unwilling to let a right or principle be weakened
senses.definitionCN: 不肯让自己的权利或原则被削弱
senses.example: They were jealous of their independence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们非常珍视自己的独立。
senses.why: A community guarding its rights watches them as closely as a jealous keeper guards a door.
senses.whyCN: 守护权利的群体，就像小心看守门的守卫一样看得极紧。

intro.en: Jealous came through Old French gelos from Greek zelos, then Latin zelus, meaning eager rivalry or zeal.
intro.cn: jealous 经古法语 gelos 来自希腊语 zelos、拉丁语 zelus，原义为热烈争胜或热忱。

items.en: zelos meant eager rivalry, zeal, or jealousy.
items.cn: zelos 意为热烈的争胜、热忱或嫉妒。

items.en: zelus kept the same range of eager feeling.
items.cn: zelus 保留了同样一串热切的情感义。

items.en: gelos narrowed the word toward jealousy and love.
items.cn: gelos 把词义收窄到嫉妒与爱情上。

items.en: English took jelus or gelous as an adjective.
items.cn: 英语借入 jelus、gelous 作形容词。

items.en: The same Greek root also gave zeal and zealous.
items.cn: 同一个希腊词根还生出 zeal 与 zealous。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jealous family and the zealous cousin; the near-meaning group holds envy and suspicion.
note.cn: 形近组是 jealous 词族与 zealous 这一同源近亲；近义组收羡慕与猜疑相关词。

entries.definition: The feeling of being jealous.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -y 构成的名词，义为「嫉妒」。

entries.definition: In a jealous or watchful way.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「嫉妒地；小心地」。

entries.definition: Full of energy for a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 同源形容词，义为「热心的」，词根同为希腊 zelos。

entries.definition: Wanting what another person has.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「羡慕的、嫉妒的」，更侧重羡慕。

entries.definition: Not trusting someone's honesty.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「多疑的」，强调不信任。

entries.definition: Wishing to control someone's attention.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「占有欲强的」，常用于关系。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie jealous to the Greek root that also produced zeal and zealous.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 jealous 系到同样生出 zeal、zealous 的希腊词根上。

normal.en: Greek zelos meant eager rivalry.
normal.cn: 希腊语 zelos 意为热烈争胜。

normal.en: Zeal and zealous share the same root.
normal.cn: zeal 与 zealous 共用同一词根。

normal.en: Jealous of is the usual pattern.
normal.cn: jealous of 是常见的搭配。

normal.en: Old French gelos pointed the word at love.
normal.cn: 古法语 gelos 把词义指向爱情。

normal.en: To guard jealously is to watch very closely.
normal.cn: guard jealously 就是看得极紧。

abstract.en: Jealousy counts what someone else is holding.
abstract.cn: 嫉妒在数别人手里有的东西。

abstract.en: The tight hand on a cup is the whole feeling.
abstract.cn: 把杯子握紧的那只手就是全部感受。

abstract.en: Watching a door and watching a person look alike.
abstract.cn: 看住门和看住一个人，动作是一样的。

examples.en: She was jealous of her sister's success.
examples.cn: 她嫉妒姐姐的成功。

examples.en: Try not to get jealous when he talks to others.
examples.cn: 他跟别人说话时尽量别吃醋。

examples.en: The country is jealous of its independence.
examples.cn: 这个国家珍视自己的独立。

root: 希腊语 zelos「热烈争胜；热忱」→ 拉丁语 zelus → 古法语 gelos「嫉妒」→ 中古英语 jelus → 现代英语 jealous。同族有 jealousy、jealously，同源近亲 zeal、zealous。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: wanting another's goods, fearing a rival in love, guarding one's own, mild envy, and valuing a right.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：想要别人之物、怕爱人被抢、守护自己的东西、轻微羡慕，以及珍视某种权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tightening on a cup while someone reaches toward a friend.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人朝你的朋友伸手，你把杯子握得更紧。

branches.en: THE CAR: a new car shining in a neighbour's drive.
branches.cn: 新车这条线：邻居车道上发亮的新车。

branches.en: THE PARTY: a long talk with an old friend.
branches.cn: 聚会这条线：跟老朋友的长时间闲聊。

branches.en: THE TEAM: a manager protecting working hours.
branches.cn: 团队这条线：经理护着工作时间。

branches.en: THE HOLIDAY: a long break that is envied.
branches.cn: 假期这条线：让人羡慕的长假。

branches.en: THE COUNTRY: independence watched day and night.
branches.cn: 国家这条线：日日夜夜守着的独立。

intro.cn: jealous 是经法语借入的形容词，英语在后面加了名词、副词和 -ness 词尾。

definition_zh: 嫉妒；嫉妒心；吃醋；羡慕
definition_en: the feeling of being unhappy because someone has something you want, or may take someone you love
core_image: 一个人站在门外，从门缝往里看，屋里的人在笑
scene: 她看到朋友的照片里多了一张陌生的脸，心一下沉下去。A wave of jealousy swept over her when she saw the photo.
sceneCN: 这里 jealousy 是「嫉妒」（第 1 个义项：因别人拥有自己想要之物而不快），句意为看到那张照片时一阵嫉妒涌上来。画面里的物件：手机里的照片、陌生的脸。

pos.zh: 名词：嫉妒；嫉妒心；吃醋

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词基础形式，义为「嫉妒的」
由 jealous 加 -ly 构成，义为「嫉妒地」
由 jealous 加 -ness 构成，义为「嫉妒的状态」

senses.title: Resentment at another's goods
senses.definition: the unhappy feeling that comes from seeing someone else have what you want
senses.definitionCN: 看到别人拥有你想要的而产生的难受心情
senses.example: Jealousy made him refuse to congratulate her.
senses.exampleCN: 嫉妒使他不肯向她道贺。
senses.why: The noun names the emotion itself, while the adjective names the person who feels it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指情感本身，而形容词指感到这种情感的人。

senses.title: Fear of a rival
senses.definition: the anxious feeling that someone you love prefers another person
senses.definitionCN: 担心所爱的人更喜欢别人的焦虑心情
senses.example: His jealousy grew every time she mentioned the new colleague.
senses.exampleCN: 她每提一次那位新同事，他的醋意就多一分。
senses.why: This is the narrowest and oldest emotional sense, coming from the word for a rival.
senses.whyCN: 这是最窄也最古老的情感义，来自表示情敌的那个词。

senses.title: Envy of a position
senses.definition: a milder feeling of wanting the situation another person enjoys
senses.definitionCN: 较轻的、想要别人所处境况的心情
senses.example: There is some jealousy behind his kind words.
senses.exampleCN: 他好话背后有一点羡慕。
senses.why: English lets the same noun cover a whole range from admiration to resentment.
senses.whyCN: 英语让这个名词覆盖从钦佩到怨恨的整段区间。

senses.title: A watchful protectiveness
senses.definition: careful guarding of something one values, without anger
senses.definitionCN: 对珍视之物的谨慎守护，不带怒意
senses.example: The rules were kept with a certain jealousy.
senses.exampleCN: 这些规矩被相当小心的珍视着。
senses.why: Guarding closely is the noun's older, cooler sense of keeping watch.
senses.whyCN: 紧守不放是这个名词较古老也较冷静的「看护」义。

senses.title: An instance of the feeling
senses.definition: a particular occasion or cause of such a feeling, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式指具体的嫉妒事件或让人嫉妒的原因
senses.example: The old jealousies between the two villages never died.
senses.exampleCN: 两个村子之间旧日的嫉妒从未消失。
senses.why: Plural use turns the mood into countable events with a history.
senses.whyCN: 复数把这种情绪变成有来历、可数的事件。

intro.en: Jealousy follows the adjective jealous, from Old French gelos and Latin zelus, itself from Greek zelos.
intro.cn: jealousy 顺着形容词 jealous 而来，源头是古法语 gelos、拉丁语 zelus，更远是希腊语 zelos。

items.en: zelos named eager rivalry and zeal.
items.cn: zelos 指热烈的争胜与热忱。

items.en: zelus was the Latin form used in church and poetic writing.
items.cn: zelus 是其拉丁形式，见于宗教与诗文。

items.en: gelos named a jealous person and gelosie the feeling.
items.cn: gelos 指嫉妒的人，gelosie 指这种心情。

items.en: English borrowed jealousy as the noun of the emotion.
items.cn: 英语借入 jealousy 作为这种情感的名词。

items.en: The plural jealousies names repeated outbreaks of the feeling.
items.cn: 复数 jealousies 指这种情感反复出现。

note.en: The look-alike group is jealous plus its endings; the near-meaning group holds envy and distrust.
note.cn: 形近组是 jealous 及其词尾形式；近义组收羡慕与不信任相关词。

entries.definition: Feeling unhappy about another's good fortune.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「嫉妒的」，本词的基础形式。

entries.definition: In a jealous or watchful manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「嫉妒地；小心地」，同族。

entries.definition: The quality of being jealous.
entries.definitionCN: 由 jealous 加 -ness 构成，义为「嫉妒的状态」。

entries.definition: The wish to have what another has.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「羡慕；嫉妒」，更侧重想要。

entries.definition: Bitter anger at unfair treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「怨恨」，起因是不公而非比较。

entries.definition: A lack of trust in someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「不信任」，没有对比成分。

normalIntro.en: These hooks place the noun after the adjective and keep the picture of watching a door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把名词放在形容词之后，并保留「从门缝里看」的画面。

normal.en: Jealousy is the noun built on jealous.
normal.cn: jealousy 是在 jealous 上构成的名词。

normal.en: Greek zelos gave zeal and jealousy alike.
normal.cn: 希腊语 zelos 同时生出 zeal 与 jealousy。

normal.en: A fit of jealousy is a sudden burst of it.
normal.cn: a fit of jealousy 就是一阵嫉妒。

normal.en: Out of jealousy, he said nothing.
normal.cn: 出于嫉妒，他什么也没说。

normal.en: Repeated outbursts become jealousies in the plural.
normal.cn: 反复发作就能用复数 jealousies。

abstract.en: Jealousy is a scale that weighs only other people.
abstract.cn: 嫉妒是一台只称别人的秤。

abstract.en: The room is warm and the watcher is outside.
abstract.cn: 屋里是暖的，看的人在外面。

abstract.en: Envy wants the thing; jealousy fears the loss.
abstract.cn: 羡慕想要那个东西，嫉妒怕失去。

examples.en: He could not hide his jealousy at the news.
examples.cn: 听到这消息他藏不住嫉妒。

examples.en: Professional jealousy is common among writers.
examples.cn: 作家之间同行相嫉很常见。

examples.en: Their old jealousies were finally forgotten.
examples.cn: 他们旧日的那些嫉妒终于被忘了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「急了谁」—— 嫉妒一起，心里急得不知该怪谁

root: 希腊语 zelos「争胜；热忱」→ 拉丁语 zelus → 古法语 gelosie → 中古英语 jealousy。同族有 jealous、jealously、jealousness，同源近亲 zeal。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: resentment at another's goods, fear of a rival, mild envy, a watchful protectiveness, and countable outbreaks of the feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：对别人所得的怨恨、怕情敌的吃醋、轻微羡慕、小心的珍视，以及可数的嫉妒事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watcher outside a lit window watching people laugh.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗外的人看着屋里的人在笑。

branches.en: THE NEWS: no word of congratulation offered.
branches.cn: 好消息这条线：一句道贺也没说。

branches.en: THE COLLEAGUE: one name repeated too often.
branches.cn: 同事这条线：一个名字被提得太多次。

branches.en: THE COMPLIMENT: praise with a hard edge.
branches.cn: 称赞这条线：好话里带刺。

branches.en: THE RULES: kept with unusual care.
branches.cn: 规矩这条线：被格外小心地守。

branches.en: THE VILLAGES: quarrels that never ended.
branches.cn: 村子这条线：从未结束的旧怨。

intro.en: Jealousy is the adjective jealous with a noun ending; the root itself is Greek via Latin and French.
intro.cn: jealousy 是形容词 jealous 加名词词尾，词根本身经法语、拉丁语来自希腊语。

latinIntro.en: Latin zelus supplies the stem behind the English -ous form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 zelus 提供了英语 -ous 形式背后的词干。

definition_zh: 果冻；胶状物；肉冻；果酱（美式）
definition_en: a soft, clear, sweet food that shakes, or any substance with a soft, thick, semi-solid texture
core_image: 一盘果冻轻轻一晃，整块都在颤，却没散开
scene: 孩子用勺子碰了碰盘子里的果冻，整块晃动起来。The jelly wobbled on the plate as the table shook.
sceneCN: 这里 jelly 是「果冻」（第 1 个义项：柔软透明、会晃动的甜食），句意为桌子一震动，盘子里的果冻就晃起来。画面里的物件：盘子、勺子、果冻。

pos.zh: 名词：果冻；胶状物；肉冻

derivatives.zh: 由 jelly 加 -ed 构成，义为「冻状的；结成果冻的」
由 jelly 与 like 复合，义为「果冻状的」
由 jelly 与 fish 复合，义为「水母」

senses.title: A wobbly sweet food
senses.definition: a soft, transparent sweet food made from fruit juice and gelatine or a similar setting agent
senses.definitionCN: 用果汁加明胶或类似凝固剂做成、柔软透明的甜食
senses.example: The children ate jelly with cream.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们吃了加奶油的果冻。
senses.why: The food sense is the central one and the base of all the images that follow.
senses.whyCN: 食物义是核心，也是后面所有意象的底本。

senses.title: Any soft set substance
senses.definition: a substance that is soft, thick, and partly solid, holding its shape only loosely
senses.definitionCN: 柔软、浓稠、半固体的物质，只能勉强保持形状
senses.example: The medicine comes as a clear jelly in a tube.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药是装在软管里的透明凝胶。
senses.why: The texture, not the fruit, is what the word names here, so it spreads to gels.
senses.whyCN: 这里指的不是水果而是质地，于是词义扩展到各种凝胶。

senses.title: Meat set in its juices
senses.definition: meat cooked and cooled in its own juices until it forms a firm mass
senses.definitionCN: 肉在自身汤汁中煮熟冷却后凝成的一块
senses.example: Sunday lunch ended with cold tongue in jelly.
senses.exampleCN: 周日的午餐以舌头肉冻收尾。
senses.why: Meat set in aspic uses the same setting action as fruit jelly, so the name carried over.
senses.whyCN: 肉冻与水果冻用的是同一种凝固定型，名字就随之搬了过来。

senses.title: A fruit spread in America
senses.definition: in American English, a clear fruit spread similar to jam but smoother
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语里指比果酱更细腻透明的果摊
senses.example: He put grape jelly on his toast.
senses.exampleCN: 他在吐司上抹了葡萄酱。
senses.why: American usage keeps a separate name for the clear kind, while British usage does not.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法给透明的这种留了单独的称呼，英式则不然。

senses.title: A body weakened by fear
senses.definition: used in phrases to say that legs or nerves have gone weak and soft
senses.definitionCN: 用于说法中表示腿或神经变得发软无力
senses.example: His legs turned to jelly before the speech.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲前他的腿都软了。
senses.why: The metaphor map is direct: something firm changes into something that shakes.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻很直接：原本坚硬的东西变成了会晃的东西。

intro.en: Jelly came through Old French gelee from Latin gelata, "frozen, congealed", from gelare, "to freeze".
intro.cn: jelly 经古法语 gelee 来自拉丁语 gelata「冻结的、凝住的」，其动词是 gelare「使冻结」。

items.en: gelare meant to freeze or to congeal.
items.cn: gelare 意为使冻结、使凝结。

items.en: gelata was the feminine past participle, meaning frozen.
items.cn: gelata 是阴性过去分词，意为冻结的。

items.en: gelee meant a frost or a jelly made by setting liquid.
items.cn: gelee 意为霜冻，也指液体凝成的冻。

items.en: English took jelly for a food set into a soft solid.
items.cn: 英语借入 jelly，指凝成软固体的食物。

items.en: The word spread to gels, meat jellies, and even jellyfish.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到凝胶、肉冻，甚至水母。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jelly- family; the near-meaning group holds other set foods and soft substances.
note.cn: 形近组是 jelly- 词族；近义组收其他凝固食品与柔软物质。

entries.definition: Set in a jelly.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「做成冻的」。

entries.definition: A soft sea animal with a bell-shaped body.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「水母」，身体软似果冻。

entries.definition: To set into a firm mass.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「凝固」；jelly 由同一个凝固概念而来。

entries.definition: Fruit boiled with sugar into a thick spread.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「果酱」，带果肉，比 jelly 粗。

entries.definition: A bitter spread made from citrus fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「柑橘果酱」，常带皮。

entries.definition: A thick semi-solid substance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「凝胶」，多用于化妆品与药品。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Latin verb to freeze into plates, tubes, and nervous legs.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语「冻结」走到盘子、软管和发软的腿。

normal.en: Latin gelare means to freeze.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 gelare 意为使冻结。

normal.en: Latin gelata meant frozen or congealed.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 gelata 意为冻结的、凝住的。

normal.en: French gelee named both frost and fruit jelly.
normal.cn: 法语 gelee 既指霜冻也指果冻。

normal.en: His legs turned to jelly means he was very afraid.
normal.cn: His legs turned to jelly 意为非常害怕。

normal.en: A jellyfish is a fish made of jelly.
normal.cn: 水母就是一团果冻做成的鱼。

abstract.en: Jelly holds a shape only while nothing pushes it.
abstract.cn: 果冻只在没人推的时候才保住形状。

abstract.en: To set is to let a liquid decide to stand.
abstract.cn: 凝固就是让液体决定站起来。

abstract.en: A firm thing that starts to shake has turned to jelly.
abstract.cn: 坚硬的东西开始晃，就是变成软冻了。

examples.en: The jelly shook when the plate was moved.
examples.cn: 盘子一动，果冻就晃起来。

examples.en: She made raspberry jelly for the children.
examples.cn: 她给孩子们做了覆盆子果冻。

examples.en: His knees felt like jelly after the run.
examples.cn: 跑完之后他的膝盖软得像果冻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「结离」—— 果汁结了冻，离开盘子还会自己晃

root: 拉丁语 gelare「使冻结」→ gelata「冻结的」→ 古法语 gelee「冻；果冻」→ 中古英语 jelly。同族有 jellied、jellyfish，同源动词 jell。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a wobbly sweet food, any soft set gel, meat set in its juices, an American fruit spread, and weak legs.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：会晃的甜食、任何柔软的凝胶、肉冻、美式果酱，以及发软无力的腿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate of jelly trembling all over without falling apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盘果冻整体颤动却没有散开。

branches.en: THE DESSERT: cream spooned over red jelly.
branches.cn: 甜点这条线：红色果冻上浇着奶油。

branches.en: THE TUBE: clear gel for a burn.
branches.cn: 软管这条线：治烫伤的透明凝胶。

branches.en: THE SUNDAY TABLE: cold tongue in its own juices.
branches.cn: 周日餐桌这条线：凝在汤汁里的舌头肉。

branches.en: THE TOAST: grape spread in an American kitchen.
branches.cn: 吐司这条线：美国厨房里的葡萄酱。

branches.en: THE STAGE: legs going soft before a speech.
branches.cn: 舞台这条线：演讲前发软的腿。

intro.en: Jelly is a French reshaping of a Latin participle; English compounds and endings come later.
intro.cn: jelly 是拉丁分词在法语里的改写，后面的复合与词尾是英语加的。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb gelare and its participle gelata sit behind the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 gelare 及其分词 gelata 是整个词族的底子。

items.example: The stem of gelare and gelata.

items.exampleCN: 英语写作 jelly，而非 gelee。

definition_zh: 喷气式飞机；喷射；喷嘴；（液体或气体的）一股
definition_en: a fast aircraft driven by jet engines, or a strong narrow stream of liquid or gas forced out of a small opening
core_image: 一股水从细口喷出，笔直射得很远
scene: 机场跑道上一架飞机加速，机尾拉出一条长烟。The jet climbed into the clouds within a minute.
sceneCN: 这里 jet 是「喷气式飞机」（第 1 个义项：靠喷气发动机高速飞行的飞机），句意为一分钟内那架喷气机就爬升进了云层。画面里的物件：跑道、机尾的烟、云层。

pos.zh: 名词：喷气式飞机；喷射；喷嘴；一股
动词：乘喷气机飞行；喷出
形容词：喷气式的；乌黑发亮的

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「喷出的；乘喷气机旅行的」
由 jet 加 -ing 构成，义为「喷射」
与 jet 同源的借词，义为「突堤；码头」

senses.title: A stream forced out
senses.definition: a strong narrow stream of liquid or gas pushed out of a small opening
senses.definitionCN: 从细口被压出的一股强而窄的液体或气体
senses.example: A jet of steam rose from the kettle.
senses.exampleCN: 水壶里喷出一股蒸汽。
senses.why: The stream sense is the oldest, from a French verb meaning to throw out.
senses.whyCN: 射流义最古老，来自法语里表示「抛出」的动词。

senses.title: The nozzle itself
senses.definition: the small opening or pipe through which such a stream comes out
senses.definitionCN: 喷出这股流的细口或管子
senses.example: Clean the jet under the tap.
senses.exampleCN: 在水龙头下把喷嘴冲干净。
senses.why: The opening is named by what comes out of it, a common shift in English.
senses.whyCN: 开口借由从它出来的东西得名，这是英语里常见的转义。

senses.title: An engine that pushes by gas
senses.definition: an engine that produces forward thrust by forcing hot gas backward
senses.definitionCN: 把高温气体向后喷出来获得推力的发动机
senses.example: The jet of the plane roared during take-off.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机起飞时喷气发动机轰鸣起来。
senses.why: The machine works exactly by making a jet, so the word names engine and aircraft together.
senses.whyCN: 这台机器正是靠制造射流工作，于是这个词同时指发动机和飞机。

senses.title: An aircraft with such engines
senses.definition: a plane driven by jet engines, especially a fast passenger plane
senses.definitionCN: 由喷气发动机驱动的飞机，尤指快速客机
senses.example: They took a jet to the coast for the weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 他们周末坐喷气机去了海边。
senses.why: In everyday speech jet means the plane itself, the machine standing for the whole object.
senses.whyCN: 日常语里 jet 就指飞机本身，机器代指了整个物件。

senses.title: Deep glossy black
senses.definition: used before a colour word, especially black, for a deep shining shade
senses.definitionCN: 用在颜色词前，尤其 black，表示深沉发亮的颜色
senses.example: Her hair was jet black in the light.
senses.exampleCN: 她的头发在光下乌黑发亮。
senses.why: The dark shiny lignite called jet gave this colour sense through stone jewellery.
senses.whyCN: 一种叫 jet 的乌黑光亮褐煤，通过石饰带来了这个颜色义。

intro.en: Jet for a stream comes from French jeter, "to throw", from Latin jactare; the black stone jet is a separate word.
intro.cn: 表示射流的 jet 来自法语 jeter「投掷」，其根是拉丁语 jactare；乌黑的宝石 jet 则是另一个词。

items.en: jactare meant to throw or toss repeatedly.
items.cn: jactare 意为反复投掷、抛。

items.en: jeter meant to throw or cast.
items.cn: jeter 意为投、抛。

items.en: English formed jet as the stream thrown out.
items.cn: 英语造出 jet，指被抛出的那一股。

items.en: jet came to name the nozzle and later the pushing action of gas.
items.cn: jet 先指喷嘴，后来指气体向后推的动作。

items.en: The jet engine gave the word its aircraft sense.
items.cn: 喷气发动机给了这个词「飞机」义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jet- family; the near-meaning group holds words for planes and streams.
note.cn: 形近组是 jet- 词族；近义组收飞机与射流相关词。

entries.definition: A structure built out into the water.
entries.definitionCN: 与 jet 同源的名词，义为「突堤；码头」。

entries.definition: Sprayed out, or travelled by jet.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「喷出的；乘喷气机的」。

entries.definition: The act of sending out a stream.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「喷射」，同族名词。

entries.definition: Any flying machine, with or without jet engines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「飞机」，最中性的统称。

entries.definition: Liquid scattered in fine drops.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「喷雾」，比 jet 更散。

entries.definition: A continuous flow of liquid or gas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「流」，比 jet 更宽、更连续。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the throwing verb into nozzles and airports, keeping the black stone apart.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从「投掷」的动词走到喷嘴和机场，并把乌黑宝石那条线分开。

normal.en: French jeter means to throw.
normal.cn: 法语 jeter 意为投、抛。

normal.en: Latin jactare means to toss about.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jactare 意为反复抛掷。

normal.en: A jet of water shoots from a small hole.
normal.cn: 一股水从小孔射出。

normal.en: A jet engine pushes gas backward to go forward.
normal.cn: 喷气发动机把气体向后喷以获得向前的推力。

normal.en: Jet black comes from the shiny black stone jet.
normal.cn: jet black 来自乌黑光亮的宝石 jet。

abstract.en: A jet is a narrow line of liquid that refuses to spread.
abstract.cn: 射流是一道拒绝散开的窄线。

abstract.en: What pushes gas back is pushed forward.
abstract.cn: 往后推气的东西自己被往前推。

abstract.en: A stream and a stone share a spelling but not a history.
abstract.cn: 一股流与一块宝石拼写相同，来历却不同。

examples.en: A jet of hot water hit the wall.
examples.cn: 一股热水冲到了墙上。

examples.en: The jet crossed the Atlantic in six hours.
examples.cn: 这架喷气机六小时飞越大西洋。

examples.en: She wore a jet black dress.
examples.cn: 她穿了一条乌黑的裙子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「急特」—— 气急急地特快一喷，飞得又高又快

root: 拉丁语 jactare「反复投掷」→ 古法语 jeter「投、抛」→ 英语 jet「射流；喷嘴」→ 喷气发动机与喷气机。乌黑宝石 jet 另出一源。同族有 jetted、jetting、jetty。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a forced stream, the nozzle, a jet engine, a jet aircraft, and deep glossy black.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：被压出的射流、喷嘴、喷气发动机、喷气式飞机，以及乌黑发亮的颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard straight line of water shot from a small hole.
core.cn: 核心意象：从细孔射出的又直又硬的一股水。

branches.en: THE KETTLE: steam hissing out of a hole.
branches.cn: 水壶这条线：蒸汽从孔里嘶出来。

branches.en: THE TAP: a small nozzle rinsed clean.
branches.cn: 水龙头这条线：冲干净的喷嘴。

branches.en: THE RUNWAY: roaring gas lifting a plane.
branches.cn: 跑道这条线：轰鸣的气体把飞机抬起来。

branches.en: THE LIGHT: shining black hair.
branches.cn: 光这条线：乌黑发亮的头发。

branches.en: THE JEWELLER: the same black stone sold in a shop window.
branches.cn: 珠宝商这条线：橱窗里出售的同一块黑石。

intro.en: Jet is a French borrowing from a Latin verb of throwing; English added the verb endings and compounds.
intro.cn: jet 是古法语借来的词，源头为拉丁语「投掷」动词，英语补上动词词尾与复合。

latinIntro.en: Latin jactare, an intensified form of jacere, supplies the stem behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jactare（jacere 的加强形式）提供了这个词背后的词干。

items.example: The core noun of the entry.

definition_zh: 宝石；珠宝；珍贵的人或物；（手表的）宝石轴承
definition_en: a precious stone worn as an ornament, or a very valuable person or thing
core_image: 丝绒盒盖一开，一颗切面石头把灯光切成许多小块
scene: 旧钟表店里，柜台深处放着一只磨旧的盒盖，里面一枚戒指在灯下发亮。The ring was set with a single small jewel.
sceneCN: 这里 jewel 是「宝石」（第 1 个义项：用作装饰的珍贵石头），句意为那枚戒指镶着一颗小宝石。画面里的物件：丝绒盒、戒指、柜台灯。

pos.zh: 名词：宝石；珠宝；珍贵之物

derivatives.zh: 由 jewel 加 -ry 构成，义为「珠宝（总称）」
由 jewel 加 -er 构成，义为「珠宝商」
由 jewel 加 -ed 构成，义为「镶有宝石的」

senses.title: A precious stone
senses.definition: a rare stone that is cut and polished and worn as an ornament
senses.definitionCN: 稀少、经切割打磨后作为饰物佩戴的石头
senses.example: The necklace holds three old jewels.
senses.exampleCN: 这条项链嵌着三颗古宝石。
senses.why: The stone sense is the central one and the source of every figurative use.
senses.whyCN: 石头义是核心，也是所有比喻用法之源。

senses.title: Ornaments as a group
senses.definition: small precious ornaments, often set in gold or silver, taken together
senses.definitionCN: 嵌在金或银上的小件贵重饰物，常作为整体来称
senses.example: The queen's jewels are kept in the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 女王的珠宝存放在塔里。
senses.why: Set ornaments are counted by the stones they carry, so the stone name covers them.
senses.whyCN: 镶嵌饰物以其所载的石头计数，于是石头的名字把它们一并涵盖。

senses.title: A precious person or thing
senses.definition: someone or something greatly valued, spoken of as if made of stone
senses.definitionCN: 被极度看重的人或物，说时当作宝石一般
senses.example: This student is a jewel for the school.
senses.exampleCN: 这个学生是学校的一块宝。
senses.why: Calling a person a jewel sets value and rarity on them, as one does with a stone.
senses.whyCN: 把人称作 jewel，就是给他安上石头的贵重与稀有。

senses.title: A precious part of a whole
senses.definition: the most valuable or admired part of a larger thing
senses.definitionCN: 整体中最贵重或最受赞赏的部分
senses.example: The garden is the jewel of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 花园是这片庄园的明珠。
senses.why: One bright stone in a crown lends its brightness to the whole, and so does the jewel part.
senses.whyCN: 冠上一颗亮石点亮整体，最珍贵的部分也这样照亮全局。

senses.title: A bearing in a watch
senses.definition: a tiny hard stone used in a watch to reduce friction at the moving parts
senses.definitionCN: 手表里减少活动部件摩擦用的微小硬石
senses.example: A watch with many jewels keeps better time.
senses.exampleCN: 宝石轴承多的手表走时更准。
senses.why: Watchmakers used real ruby or sapphire, so the technical part kept the mineral name.
senses.whyCN: 制表匠用的确是真红宝或蓝宝石，于是这个技术部件沿用了宝石之名。

intro.en: Jewel came through Old French joel or jouel, probably from Latin jocale, "a plaything", from jocus, "jest".
intro.cn: jewel 经古法语 joel、jouel 而来，很可能源自拉丁语 jocale「玩物」，其根是 jocus「玩笑」。

items.en: jocus meant a jest or game.
items.cn: jocus 意为玩笑、游戏。

items.en: jocale named a plaything or an ornament of pleasure.
items.cn: jocale 指玩物或供赏玩的饰物。

items.en: joel or jouel named a jewel, often a woman's ornament.
items.cn: joel、jouel 指宝石，常为女子的饰物。

items.en: English took the word as juel or jewell.
items.cn: 英语借入为 juel、jewell。

items.en: The spelling settled as jewel, and the figurative senses spread.
items.cn: 拼写定为 jewel，比喻义随之普及。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jewel- family; the near-meaning group holds stones and valuables.
note.cn: 形近组是 jewel- 词族；近义组收石头与贵重物相关词。

entries.definition: Jewels and ornaments as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ry 构成，义为「珠宝（总称）」。

entries.definition: A person who sells or makes jewels.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「珠宝商」。

entries.definition: Set with jewels.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「镶宝石的」。

entries.definition: A precious or semi-precious stone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「宝石」，也可比喻珍品。

entries.definition: Something of great value kept safely.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「宝物」，不限于石头。

entries.definition: A decorative object.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「装饰品」，不一定贵重。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Latin plaything into rings, crowns, and watch bearings.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「玩物」走到戒指、王冠和手表轴承。

normal.en: Latin jocus means a jest, and jocale a plaything.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jocus 意为玩笑，jocale 意为玩物。

normal.en: Old French jouel named a lovely ornament.
normal.cn: 古法语 jouel 指可爱的饰物。

normal.en: Jewelry is the group name for jewels.
normal.cn: jewelry 是 jewelry 的总称名词。

normal.en: A jeweller sets jewels into rings.
normal.cn: jeweller 把宝石镶进戒指。

normal.en: A watch counts its jewels as bearings.
normal.cn: 手表以宝石轴承数来衡量。

abstract.en: A jewel is a stone that learned to shine.
abstract.cn: 宝石是一块学会了发亮的石头。

abstract.en: One bright stone lends light to the whole crown.
abstract.cn: 一颗亮石照亮整顶王冠。

abstract.en: Treat people as jewels and they get rare.
abstract.cn: 把人当宝石看，人便稀有起来。

examples.en: The old crown is set with rare jewels.
examples.cn: 这顶旧王冠上镶着稀有的宝石。

examples.en: This little library is the jewel of the town.
examples.cn: 这座小图书馆是镇上的明珠。

examples.en: He bought a ring with a single blue jewel.
examples.cn: 他买了一枚镶一颗蓝宝石的戒指。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「珠宝」—— 音近义近，盒盖一开就是一片亮

root: 拉丁语 jocus「玩笑」→ jocale「玩物；赏玩之饰」→ 古法语 joel／jouel → 中古英语 jewell → 现代英语 jewel。同族有 jewelry、jeweller、jewelled。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a precious stone, ornaments as a group, a precious person or thing, the finest part, and a watch bearing.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：珍贵石头、珠宝总称、宝贵的人或物、最珍贵的部分，以及手表宝石轴承。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a velvet lid opening to a tilted stone splitting the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：丝绒盒盖打开，一颗斜面的石头把光切开。

branches.en: THE RING: one small stone under a lamp.
branches.cn: 戒指这条线：灯下的一颗小石头。

branches.en: THE TOWER: a whole collection kept under guard.
branches.cn: 塔这条线：被人看守的整批珠宝。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: a student everyone values.
branches.cn: 学校这条线：人人都看重的学生。

branches.en: THE GARDEN: the finest part of an estate.
branches.cn: 花园这条线：庄园里最美的部分。

branches.en: THE WATCH: tiny ruby bearings in the works.
branches.cn: 手表这条线：机芯里的小红宝石轴承。

intro.en: Jewel is a French borrowing whose endings are English or French; the Latin root is jocus.
intro.cn: jewel 是法语借词，后续词尾属英语或法语，拉丁词根是 jocus。

latinIntro.en: Latin jocus "jest" gave jocale "plaything", the likely source of the French word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jocus「玩笑」生出 jocale「玩物」，很可能就是法语词的来源。

items.example: The form behind the French word.
